issue.title: Hoist host-scoped init planners (config, skills) out of sase init --all's per-project loop
issue.description:
Discovered while researching the Admin Center Projects-tab init feature (research
report: sase/repos/research/202609/projects_tab_init_ux/).

`run_init_onboarding_all` (src/sase/main/init_onboarding.py:493) runs
`_run_init_onboarding_result` per project inside `_working_directory`, and that
function plans and applies all four registered init specs each time. Two of the four
are host-scoped, not project-scoped: `config` plans only from the agent-owner config
snapshot (`plan_config_init` starts with `del args`, config_init_handler.py:54-56) and
`skills` targets `~/.<provider>/skills/` / the chezmoi source tree with sources loaded
via `get_all_xprompts(project="")` (init_skills_handler.py:148, _init_skills_sources.py:62-77).

Measured on apollo (research report B): a full check costs ~8.4 s of work per project,
of which config ≈ 0.8 s and skills ≈ 6.9 s (~92%) are project-independent. So an
N-project `sase init --all` redoes roughly (N-1) x 7.7 s of identical planning work.

Proposed remediation: hoist the host-scoped specs (config, skills) out of the
per-project loop — plan/apply them once before iterating projects, keeping registry
ordering guarantees (config before memory) and the single deferred chezmoi deploy
(`defer_chezmoi_deploy`, init_onboarding.py:515) intact. Per-project iteration then
runs only the memory and repo specs.

task_type_fields.proposal: sase init --all should plan and apply the two host-scoped specs (config, skills) once per run instead of once per project, cutting roughly (N-1) x 7.7 s of redundant work from an N-project run while preserving registry ordering and the single deferred chezmoi deploy.
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope: Found while researching how to invoke sase init from the Admin Center Projects tab. That feature consumes the CLI as-is; restructuring the --all coordinator loop is an orthogonal CLI performance change with its own risk surface (spec ordering, chezmoi deploy batching), so it does not belong in the TUI feature's scope.
